meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: The official position of the Polish government is that the Directive 2016/1919 has been fully transposed. However, in fact the transposition is only partial - compare comments below regarding detailed provisions of the Directive. The comments are expression of experts own assessment backed by references to Polish legal doctrine and case-law.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning the right to legal aid for:
(a)suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings; and

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
According to Polish law only a person formally charged with a crime during criminal investigation is granted a status of podejrzany and provided with certain rights including a right to access to a lawyer, right to remain silent, right to legal aid etc. This charging decision however, can be considered only as a preliminary charging decision and does not involve the court in any way. In particular, it cannot be considered as equal to filing a case with a court with an aim to accuse a person with a crime. This is done later at the end of criminal investigation in the form of indictment which makes podejrzany to become oskarżony - a party to court proceedings with all rights available to him or her at this stage of criminal process. 

Note that both colloquially and in official wording of Polish version of Directive the word podejrzany is translated from Polish to English as suspect. This causes misunderstanding and misinterpretation of whether Directives are properly and fully implemented or not.

In the light of the above, one can assume, as it is done so by the Polish government, that the Polish criminal procedure remains in compliance with the EU Directive since podejrzany in Polish legal system is guaranteed all rights provided in Directives for the suspect. But such an interpretation is inconsistent with the meaning of the concept of a suspect as used in Directives. The Polish definition of podejrzany does not encompass the individual against whom the criminal investigation is aimed being arrested or searched but not yet formally charged with a crime. The Polish law provides for such an individual a separate name i.e. osoba podejrzana (translated directly as suspected person) and does not provide for her the same protection that the podejrzany is normally provided with. Some limited protection is only provided in case osoba podejrzana is arrested. E.g. she may be assisted by a lawyer free of charge, but the latter has status of legal counsel not a defence counsel. The main difference is the scope of legal privilege available for the individual. The defence counsel cannot be questioned as witness in relation to his or her contact with the client, whereas the legal counsel can be questioned as witness in relation to his or her contact with the client (excluding cases where he or she advises arrested person). Moreover, the legal counsel does not have unlimited right to participate in questioning or other actions undertaken by the investigating authorities. 

As a result, it should be acknowledge that the Polish law does not remain in full compliance with the EU Directives since the suspect who is osoba podejrzana (until formal preliminary charges are laid out against her during investigation) is not entitled to the same protection that is given to podejrzany. In order to assume that the EU Directives are properly and fully implemented in Poland the guarantees provided for the suspect should be extended also to those individuals who acquired status of osoba podejrzana and are not yet preliminarily charged with a crime.

items.text: (b)persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (requested persons).
items.comment: See comments to Article 5.

items.text: 2. This Directive complements Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800. Nothing in this Directive shall be interpreted as limiting the rights provided for in those Directives.

items.heading: Article 2
items.comment:

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU and who are:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: (a)deprived of liberty;
(b)required to be assisted by a lawyer in accordance with Union or national law; or
(c)required or permitted to attend an investigative or evidence-gathering act, including as a minimum the following:
(i)identity parades;
(ii)confrontations;
(iii)reconstructions of the scene of a crime.
2. This Directive also applies, upon arrest in the executing Member State, to requested persons who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU.

3. This Directive also applies, under the same conditions as provided for in paragraph 1, to persons who were not initially suspects or accused persons but become suspects or accused persons in the course of questioning by the police or by another law enforcement authority.
4. Without prejudice to the right to a fair trial, in respect of minor offences:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: (a)where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed or referred to such a court; or

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: (b)where deprivation of liberty cannot be imposed as a sanction;
this Directive applies only to the proceedings before a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters.
In any event, this Directive applies when a decision on detention is taken, and during detention, at any stage of the proceedings until the conclusion of the proceedings.
For the purposes of this Directive, ‘legal aid’ means funding by a Member State of the assistance of a lawyer, enabling the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer.
items.heading: Article 3
items.comment: The term 'legal aid' is understood in Poland in accordance with the definition included in Article 3. There is no legal definition of that term in any legally binding act, but the legal doctrine is unanimous on that matter.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego

provisions.textEn:
§ 1. An accused, who does not have a defence counsel of his own choice, may request the appointment of a defence counsel ex officio, if he can duly prove that he is unable to bear the costs of defence without prejudice to the necessary maintenance of himself, or his family.

§ 1a. The provision of § 1a applies accordingly to the appointment of the defence counsel for the purpose of conducting specific procedural action.

§ 2. A person, who is not a party to the proceedings, may appoint a legal counsel if his interest in the proceedings so requires.

§ 3. The court, and in preparatory proceedings the public prosecutor, may refuse to admit the attorney referred to in § 2 to participation in the proceedings, if in their opinion it is not necessary for the protection of the interests of the person, who is not a party to the proceedings.

§ 1. Only an advocate, a legal advisor or a counsel of the Office of the General Counsel to the Republic of Poland may act as an legal counsel. Articles 77, 78, 81a § 1-3, 83, 84 and 86 § 2 and provisions issued on the basis of Article 81a § 4 apply accordingly to the legal counsel.

items.comment:
1) In relation to persons after the formal presentation of charges according to Polish CCP (podejrzany) and people accused before the court - no need for transposition.

Article 78 CCP

§ 1. An accused, who does not have a defence counsel of his own choice, may request the appointment of a defence counsel ex officio, if he can duly prove that he is unable to bear the costs of defence without prejudice to the necessary maintenance of himself, or his family.

§ 1a. The provision of § 1a applies accordingly to the appointment of the defence counsel for the purpose of conducting specific procedural action.

 

2) In relation to persons, to whom charges were not formally presented – no transposition.

Article 87 CCP.

§ 2. A person, who is not a party to the proceedings, may appoint a legal counsel if his interest in the proceedings so requires.

§ 3. The court, and in preparatory proceedings the public prosecutor, may refuse to admit the attorney referred to in § 2 to participation in the proceedings, if in their opinion it is not necessary for the protection of the interests of the person, who is not a party to the proceedings.

 

Article 88 CCP

§ 1. Only an advocate, a legal advisor or a counsel of the Office of the General Counsel to the Republic of Poland may act as an legal counsel. Articles 77, 78, 81a § 1-3, 83, 84 and 86 § 2 and provisions issued on the basis of Article 81a § 4 apply accordingly to the legal counsel.


Persons, to whom charges were not presented are not equally protected as persons after formal presentation of charges (in Polish law to be granted a formal status of suspect – podejrzany – who is a party to preparatory proceedings, the investigating authority has to present charges to person; before that even if investigative measures are taken against a person (e.g. arrest, search) and a person is a suspect in the sense of the Directive in Poland he or she is named osoba podejrzana ­­– suspected person and does not have a status of party and its rights). They may be assisted by lawyer free of charge, but the latter has status of legal counsel not a defence counsel. The main difference is in the scope of legal privilege. The defence counsel cannot be questioned as witness in relation to his or her contact with the client, whereas the legal counsel can be questioned as witness in relation to his or her contact with the client (excluding cases where he or she advices arrested person). Moreover the legal counsel does not have unlimited right to participate in questioning or other actions undertaken by the investigating authorities. The court, and in preparatory proceedings the public prosecutor, may refuse to admit the legal counsel to participate in the proceedings, if in their opinion it is not necessary for the protection of the interests of the person, who is to be represented (Article 87 § 3 CCP).


3) There is no expressly stated requirement of “when the interests of justice so require” in Polish law (as in Article 4(1) of the Directive)

However it should be mentioned that the Polish CCP provides for so-called mandatory defence (applicable to all persons after formal the presentation of charges irrespective of their financial situation), which may indirectly be qualified as an expression of acknowledging the premise “when the interests of justice so require”.


Article 79 CCP

§ 1. In the criminal proceedings, the accused must be assisted by a defence counsel if:

1) he has not attained eighteen years of age,

2) he is deaf, mute or blind,

3) there is a justified doubt whether his ability to comprehend the meaning of his deed or to control his behaviour was not, at the time of committing the offence, excluded or significantly reduced,

4) there is a justified doubt whether the condition of his mental health allows him to participate in the proceedings or to conduct his defence in an independent and reasonable manner.

§ 2. The accused must also have a defence counsel if the court deems it necessary due to other circumstances impeding the defence.

items.comment:
1) Means test is used in case of persons after formal presentation of charges.

As explained in comments to Article 4(1) of the Directive the merit test as such is not applied. However the provisions concerning mandatory defence may be treated as referring to “interest of justice”.


2) Means test and merits test are used for suspects who were not presented charges.

The Article 87 § 2 CCP provides that a person, who is not a party to the proceedings, may appoint an attorney if his interest in the proceedings so requires.

So apart from the requirement to duly prove that the person applying for legal aid is unable to bear the costs of defence without prejudice to the necessary maintenance of himself, or his family, it has also to be assessed whether the assistance of lawyer is needed for the protection of the interests of that person.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.

items.comment: The provisions in the CCP does not mention any specific criteria (means test) that has to be taken under consideration when deciding on granting free legal aid. However both the general wording of Article 78 CCP and the case law of the Supreme Court (e.g. resolution of the Supreme Court of 17.07.2014, V KZ 26/14, LEX no. 1487098) allows to conclude that the Directive’s standard is satisfied.

items.text: 4. Where a Member State applies a merits test, it shall take into account the seriousness of the criminal offence, the complexity of the case and the severity of the sanction at stake, in order to determine whether the interests of justice require legal aid to be granted. In any event, the merits test shall be deemed to have been met in the following situations:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
In cases of persons to whom charges were not presented the standard derived from Directive is not met.

 

There is a dispute in the legal doctrine as to what are the criteria of granting free assistance of legal counsel. On one hand it is argued that only the means test should be applied. On the other it is argued that since according to Article 87 § 2 CCP a person, who is not a party to the proceedings, may appoint a legal counsel if his interest in the proceedings so requires, merits test should be also applied. The latter point of view is correct. Assuming so, that assessment does not satisfy at least the assumptions enlisted in letters a) and b) of Article 4(4).

 

Moreover it should be mentioned that Article 87 § 3 CCP provides that the court, and in preparatory proceedings the public prosecutor, may refuse to admit the legal counsel to participate in the proceedings, if in their opinion it is not necessary for the protection of the interests of the person, who is not a party to the proceedings. That provisions gives the prosecutor and court discretionary power to limit the effectiveness of the assistance of legal counsel. Although the above-mentioned provision does not relate to appointment of ex officio legal counsel itself it has an important impact on execution of right to be represented by lawyer and de facto affects the functioning of ex officio legal aid.

(b)during detention.

provisions.textEn:
§ 1 CCP Defence counsel ex officio is appointed from the list of defence counsels.

§ 2. The request for the appointment of a defence counsel ex officio is heard immediately by the president of the court, the court or the court referendary.

§ 3. If, in view of the circumstances, the defence should be undertaken immediately, the president of the court, the court or the court referendary immediately notifies the accused and the defence counsel in a manner specified in Article 137, of the appointment of the defence counsel ex officio.

§ 4. The Minister of Justice shall define by way of a regulation:

1) the modalities of guarantying to the accused the assistance of the defence counsel ex officio, including the modality of forming the list of defence counsels providing legal assistance ex officio and of their appointment,

2) the manner in which the request for the appointment of the defence counsel should be filed with the court and the detailed manner in which such motion should be heard,

- bearing in mind the necessity of insuring a correct course of proceedings, as well a correct realisation of the right to defence.
Article 517j § 3 and regulations enacted on the ground of Article 517j § 2 apply accordingly.

In order to make it possible for the accused to use the assistance of a defence counsel, in accelerated proceedings advocates and legal advisors shall be on duty in the time and place determined in separate provisions.

items.comment: As it is clarified in the regulation issued by the Minister of Justice the advocates and legal advisers volunteer or are appointed to be on duty in the curcuit of district court. That provision is applied accordingly to appointment of legal counsel (Article 88 § 1 CCP)

items.text: 6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.
items.comment:
The legal aid is granted for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

items.text: 2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.
items.comment:
Polish CCP does not contain any specific provisions regarding assistance of the lawyer in situation described in Article 5(2) of the Directive.

However general rules related to ex officio legal aid (as described in comments on Article 4) are applicable in criminal proceedings for the purpose of which the EAW was issued. If a defence counsel is appointed in such proceedings he or she may also assist the suspect or accused person in cases related to issuance of the EAW.

items.text: 3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.

The system of free legal aid in Poland is often criticized, because the remuneration of advocates and legal advisers is remarkably lower than the market prices for legal counselling. That may raise doubts whether the services in practice are of a adequate quality.

items.heading: Article 8

provisions.textEn: The decision of the president of the court denying the appointment of the defence counsel is subject to interlocutory appeal to the court competent to hear the case. The court’s decision denying the appointment of the defence counsel is subject to interlocutory appeal to another equivalent panel of the same court.

Only an advocate, a legal advisor or a counsel of the Office of the General Counsel to the Republic of Poland may act as an legal counsel. Articles 77, 78, 81a § 1-3, 83, 84 and 86 § 2 and provisions issued on the basis of Article 81a § 4 apply accordingly to the legal counsel.

items.comment:
The denial of free legal aid can be challenged. However, there are no other remedies available in Polish law in cases there is a violation of right to free legal aid. There is no provision obliging the investigating authorities to postpone a procedural act in order to wait for the appointment of ex officio defence counsel or legal counsel. Neither there is provision allowing evidence obtained in violation of the right to legal aid to be excluded.

The only explicit remedy is related to mandatory defence explained in Article 4(1). Lack of mandatory defence counsel in proceedings before the court causes that judgment passed, if appealed, should be ex officio quashed by the court of higher instance and the case send for retrial (Article 439 par. 1(10) CCP).

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account in the implementation of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is no provision in the Polish CCP that ensures that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account. It all depends on the approach of the investigating authorities.
